plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't depend on what others bid or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above your value risks winning and overpaying; bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' strategies or beliefs about me, my optimal action is to bid exactly my value of $35.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do—it maximizes expected profit. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so I don't need to shade my bid down to avoid overpaying. Bidding my true value of $32 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and never overpay, since payment depends only on the second-highest bid.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This holds because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $48, I should bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.
